rulings.docket_item: whether the first-person city stretch closing at Lam.1.17 must be re-spanned to close at Lam.1.16, or the span stands with a disclosed-deviation cure
rulings.grounds: Re-derived from the pointed text. First-person-singular marking stands in every verse of Lam.1.12 through Lam.1.16: כְּמַכְאֹבִ֔י and לִ֑י (oshb:Lam.1.12, byte tier); בְּעַצְמֹתַ֖י, לְרַגְלַי֙, הֱשִׁיבַ֣נִי and נְתָנַ֨נִי֙ (oshb:Lam.1.13, byte tier); פְּשָׁעַ֜י, צַוָּארִ֖י and כֹּחִ֑י (oshb:Lam.1.14, byte tier); אַבִּירַ֤י, בְּקִרְבִּ֔י, עָלַ֛י and בַּחוּרָ֑י (oshb:Lam.1.15, byte tier); and אֲנִ֣י, עֵינִ֤י and נַפְשִׁ֑י (oshb:Lam.1.16, byte tier). A complete token scan of Lam.1.17 returns ZERO first-person-singular forms: its pronominal suffixes are third-person throughout - בְּיָדֶ֗יהָ, the refrain's own לָ֔הּ, צָרָ֑יו and בֵּינֵיהֶֽם (oshb:Lam.1.17, byte tier). The refrain that closes the span therefore stands inside a third-person verse: אֵ֤ין מְנַחֵם֙ לָ֔הּ (oshb:Lam.1.17, byte tier) carries the third-person feminine suffix against the first-person suffix at the third site, אֵ֤ין מְנַחֵם֙ לִ֔י (oshb:Lam.1.21, byte tier); the contiguous two-token refrain stands in 3 verses of this poem, at 1:9, 1:17 and 1:21 (sweep: 3 verses, skeleton tier). Two tier-1 signals meet at the same verse and point opposite ways: the refrain closes the unit there, and the voice the unit is named for has already stopped. One byte correction to the material as filed, which does not change the outcome: Lam.1.16 does not OPEN on the independent pronoun - the verse opens עַל אֵ֣לֶּה (oshb:Lam.1.16, byte tier), the acrostic ayin coming from that preposition, with אֲנִ֣י standing third in the verse; those same two words also confirm that this verse's second token is the demonstrative and not a divine name, so the census entry that reads it otherwise is false. The alternative close at Lam.1.16 is not adopted: it would leave Lam.1.17 standing alone on the single pe letter, which the ruled granularity bars absent a disclosed tier-1 reason, and folding that verse forward into Lam.1.18-Lam.1.22 would move the identical third-person defect from the back of one unit to the front of the next, where first-person marking resumes immediately at מָרִ֑יתִי (oshb:Lam.1.18, byte tier; a ketiv/qere verse, disclosed because a form is spliced from it, the variant standing at the peoples-word and not at this form). The span is carried by the tier-1 refrain close; what fails is the description of it, and the disclosure is the operative remedy.

rulings.docket_item: whether the front-seam continuity claim on the Lam.1.18-Lam.1.22 span calls for a respan or a field cure
rulings.grounds: Re-derived. The front-seam neighbour Lam.1.17 carries no first-person-singular form: a complete token scan returns zero, its suffixes running בְּיָדֶ֗יהָ, צָרָ֑יו and בֵּינֵיהֶֽם (oshb:Lam.1.17, byte tier). The span's own first verse opens the first person afresh with מָרִ֑יתִי (oshb:Lam.1.18, byte tier; a ketiv/qere verse, disclosed because a form is spliced from it). So the voice RESUMES across an intervening third-person verse rather than keeping on through it, and the front-seam sentence as written asserts the stronger of the two readings. The defect is real and correctly graded low, because the span's own content is first-person throughout and both its edges verify on independent tier-1 grounds: the third refrain site carries the first-person suffix אֵ֤ין מְנַחֵם֙ לִ֔י (oshb:Lam.1.21, byte tier) against the third-person feminine suffix at the two earlier sites, and the poem's letter run closes on tav at Lam.1.22. The addressee finding also verifies against the bytes and is the sharper of the two: the span OPENS on a second-person plural imperative addressed to the peoples, שִׁמְעוּ נָ֣א (oshb:Lam.1.18, byte tier), Lam.1.19 carries no address at all, and the sustained second-person-masculine-singular address to the deity begins only at רְאֵ֨ה יְהוָ֤ה (oshb:Lam.1.20, byte tier) and runs through Lam.1.22 - so a single sustained address across the whole span is byte-false and must narrow to web:Lam.1.20-web:Lam.1.22. No span change is proposed and none is warranted: both seams sit on letter boundaries and both are argued by tier-1 signals.

consequence.spec: Proposal declined; the existing two-part work order on P01-004 stands UNCHANGED: (1) boundary_rationale reworded so the first-person voice RESUMES at web:Lam.1.18 after an intervening third-person verse, with the front-seam neighbour's person state disclosed (no first-person-singular form at web:Lam.1.17); (2) strongest_rejected_alternative narrowing the sustained address to web:Lam.1.20-web:Lam.1.22 and recording that the span opens instead on a second-person plural imperative appeal to the peoples at web:Lam.1.18. rulings.docket_item: whether the close of the second poem's opening report moves from Lam.2.9 to Lam.2.10 so the seam sits at the first-person onset in Lam.2.11
rulings.grounds: Adopted on re-derived bytes. A complete person scan of Lam.2.1 through Lam.2.10 returns zero first-person-singular forms and zero second-person forms of any gender: the ten verses run third-person throughout, with the divine agent and the city's own things and people as their subjects. The first person enters at Lam.2.11, which carries four first-person-singular pronominal suffixes - עֵינַי֙, מֵעַ֔י, כְּבֵדִ֔י and the suffix inside בַּת עַמִּ֑י (oshb:Lam.2.11, byte tier). CONTROLLING COUNT OBJECT: three is the count of the speaker's own body-part nouns in that verse; four is the count of first-person-singular pronominal suffixes, and the four-suffix census is the object carried here. That onset is a tier-1 voice change and it is one of the named voice signals of this poem; nothing of that class stands at the Lam.2.9/Lam.2.10 cut. What changes there is subject matter and grammatical subject only - and not cleanly even there, since Lam.2.9 already reports the city's human groups, her king, her princes and her prophets, before יֵשְׁב֨וּ (oshb:Lam.2.10, byte tier) opens the report of the elders and the virgins, so the cut falls inside a run of human-participant reporting rather than at its head. The cut also fails the standard the row itself applies to the interior split it sets aside, and the mark layer cannot discriminate it: this poem carries a mark at every one of its 22 verses, 21 of one type and the poem-closing type at 2:22 (sweep: 22 marked verses of 22), tier-3 weak and single-witness. Finally the cut is straddled: the two-token daughter-of-Zion formula stands at בַּת צִיּ֔וֹן (oshb:Lam.2.8, byte tier) inside it and at בַת צִיּ֔וֹן (oshb:Lam.2.10, byte tier) immediately outside it - 8 verses book-wide, 6 of them in this poem at 2:1, 2:4, 2:8, 2:10, 2:13 and 2:18 (sweep: 8 verses book-wide, skeleton tier) - so a device the span itself cites argues continuity across its own close. Moving the close to Lam.2.10 brings both of those sites inside one span and puts the seam on the only tier-1 signal in the neighbourhood. It decides no held-open question: both candidate turn-points for the narrator-to-address transition, Lam.2.11 and Lam.2.13, remain inside a single following row, so where the narrator's first person gives way to the address stays open exactly as it was.

rulings.docket_item: whether the second poem's second-person addressee chain Lam.2.13-Lam.2.19 should be re-spanned as one unit absorbing the neighbouring apostrophe rows
rulings.grounds: The addressee finding verifies exactly and the respan is still declined. Every verse of Lam.2.14 through Lam.2.17 carries second-person feminine singular addressee marking - נְבִיאַ֗יִךְ (oshb:Lam.2.14, byte tier; a ketiv/qere verse, disclosed because a form is spliced from it, the variant standing at the captivity-word and not at this form), עָלַ֤יִךְ (oshb:Lam.2.15, byte tier), א֣וֹיְבַ֔יִךְ (oshb:Lam.2.16, byte tier), צָרָֽיִךְ (oshb:Lam.2.17, byte tier) - and a complete enumeration of this poem's second-person feminine singular forms returns exactly seven consecutive verses, Lam.2.13 through Lam.2.19, and no other verse of the poem: Lam.2.12 runs third-person plural, and Lam.2.20 turns to a second-person masculine singular address to the deity at רְאֵ֤ה יְהוָה֙ with עוֹלַ֣לְתָּ (oshb:Lam.2.20, byte tier). So third-person finite verbs stand with a second-person addressee across the whole span, the third-person-report description fails at every one of its verses, and both of its seams cut the chain: the daughter-of-Jerusalem formula stands at הַבַּת֙ יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם (oshb:Lam.2.13, byte tier) and בַּ֖ת יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם (oshb:Lam.2.15, byte tier) across the front seam (sweep: 2 verses book-wide, skeleton tier), and the addressee marking runs on into Lam.2.18 and Lam.2.19 across the back. What actually changes at the front seam is the speaker's own first person dropping out - אֲעִידֵ֞ךְ and its two companion first-person prefix-conjugation verbs at oshb:Lam.2.13 (byte tier) - while the addressee marking continues unchanged. DECLINED nonetheless, and on owner law rather than against the bytes: a unit running Lam.2.13-Lam.2.19 necessarily puts a row seam at Lam.2.12/Lam.2.13, and that seam ANSWERS a question the owner holds open, whether the narrator's first person gives way to the address at Lam.2.13 or already at Lam.2.11. A ruling may adopt a span that RESPECTS a held-open region; it may not decide one. The proposed unit would also submerge the second held question inside itself - the addressee of the imperatives that open with צָעַ֥ק לִבָּ֖ם (oshb:Lam.2.18, byte tier) and run second-person feminine singular through Lam.2.19 - by removing the seam at which it is currently held. Two further tier-1 signals cut inside the proposed unit and would go unargued: the first-person drop at Lam.2.14 and the turn to second-person feminine singular imperatives at Lam.2.18. The addressee chain is a real tier-1 continuity; it is disclosed at both seams, not made into a span.

rulings.docket_item: whether the mid-stanza close at Lam.3.47 requires a span change, and what follows at that seam from the tier and form-class findings
rulings.grounds: No respan is proposed and none is warranted: the mid-stanza cut carries a disclosed tier-1 reason that verifies on the bytes - first-plural לָ֖נוּ at oshb:Lam.3.47 turning to first-singular עֵינִ֔י at oshb:Lam.3.48, both byte tier. The tier finding verifies and it is what decides the cure. Lam.3.46, Lam.3.47 and Lam.3.48 all carry the pe letter at position 16 of this poem's pinned pe-before-ayin order (tier-1 letter data), so the grouping the rejected-alternative sentence sets aside is a tier-1 letter stanza, not a mark-layer symmetry, and weighing a tier-1 person shift against it as though it were tier-3 downgrades a tier-1 counterweight. The mark layer in this poem is a separate tier-3 weak single-witness layer falling at stanza closes ONLY - 22 marked verses over the poem's 66, at 3:3, 3:6 and every third verse through 3:66 - so the mark at 3:48 corroborates that stanza close and cannot constitute it. That digit is worth naming because the controlling inventory and a summary description of it disagree: the inventory carries 89 marked verses book-wide, 22 in each of the first four poems and 1 in the fifth, and the poem-by-poem list is the controlling object; any reading on which every verse of this poem is marked is false to it. The suffix finding verifies too: the plural elements of Lam.3.46 are עָלֵ֛ינוּ (preposition plus first-plural) and אֹיְבֵֽינוּ (noun plus first-plural), and of Lam.3.47 לָ֖נוּ (preposition plus first-plural), all byte tier, while the section's plural VERBAL object suffixes stand at וַֽתִּרְדְּפֵ֔נוּ (oshb:Lam.3.43, byte tier) and תְּשִׂימֵ֖נוּ (oshb:Lam.3.45, byte tier), both outside the two verses the claim names. The translation-fidelity half is refuted on bytes: each of the four quoted lines is a verbatim substring of the verse it cites, so no fidelity mismatch exists and no work order attaches to it.

rulings.docket_item: whether the fifth poem's internal seam moves from Lam.5.11/Lam.5.12 to Lam.5.10/Lam.5.11 so the four-verse third-person run stands whole
rulings.grounds: Adopted on re-derived bytes. Lam.5.11 through Lam.5.14 each open on a bare plural human-group noun followed by a third-plural verb - נָשִׁים֙ with עִנּ֔וּ (oshb:Lam.5.11), שָׂרִים֙ (oshb:Lam.5.12), בַּחוּרִים֙ (oshb:Lam.5.13), זְקֵנִים֙ (oshb:Lam.5.14), all byte tier - and none of the four carries any first-plural form. Neither test is exclusive on its own: the same verse-initial bare plural human-group onset also stands at Lam.5.3 and Lam.5.8 (sweep: 6 verses in this poem - 5:3, 5:8, 5:11, 5:12, 5:13, 5:14, skeleton tier), and Lam.5.18 also carries no first-plural form (5 verses of Lam.5.1-Lam.5.18 carry none: 5:11, 5:12, 5:13, 5:14, 5:18). It is the CONJUNCTION of the two that is exclusive, holding in exactly four verses, Lam.5.11-Lam.5.14, the only consecutive run of any length in the poem (sweep: 4 verses of 22) - Lam.5.3 and Lam.5.8 are excluded by their own first-plural forms. That is a tier-1 participant-run repetition, and the seam as drawn cuts it after its first member, disclosed nowhere. The person shift is the only tier-1 signal in that neighbourhood: first-plural marking runs unbroken from Lam.5.1 through Lam.5.10, its last member עוֹרֵ֨נוּ֙ (oshb:Lam.5.10, byte tier), and resumes only at Lam.5.15. The unit's own cited texture does not close at Lam.5.11 either: the divine name stands at Lam.5.1, Lam.5.19 and Lam.5.21 and nowhere between (sweep: 3 verses in this poem, skeleton tier), so the lapse of direct address runs unbroken through Lam.5.18 and marks nothing at Lam.5.11. The ground offered against a cut after Lam.5.6 - no voice or addressee shift - is equally true of the close as drawn; after the move it is not, since a cut after Lam.5.6 would fall inside the first-plural catalogue (יָ֔ד at oshb:Lam.5.6, אֲבֹתֵ֤ינוּ at oshb:Lam.5.7, byte tier) while the adopted close sits on the shift itself. The mark layer corroborates nothing either way here: this poem carries one mark, the poem-closing type at Lam.5.18, and none of the other type (sweep: 1 marked verse of 22), tier-3 weak and single-witness, and absence is never counterevidence. The collateral digit and form-class findings verify and are carried into the work order below: as a petition imperative to the divine name the remember-form stands in 2 verses, Lam.3.19 and Lam.5.1, the third member of the 3-verse bare-token census being the negated third-person perfect וְלֹא זָכַ֥ר (oshb:Lam.2.1, byte tier); the look-imperative stands in 2 verses as a bare token and in 4 under the single-letter prefix test, at Lam.1.11, Lam.2.20, Lam.3.63 and Lam.5.1 (skeleton tier at both digits); and the poem's onset is a three-imperative chain, זְכֹ֤ר יְהוָה֙, then the ketiv/qere look-form הַבִּ֖יטָה, then וּרְאֵ֥ה (oshb:Lam.5.1, byte tier), not a doubled one.

rulings.docket_item: whether any further span change follows on the Lam.5.12-Lam.5.18 unit once its front seam is settled
rulings.grounds: No further span change is proposed and none is warranted. The row's back seam at Lam.5.18/Lam.5.19 sits on a tier-1 discourse turn: second-person address to the divine name reopens at אַתָּ֤ה יְהוָה֙ (oshb:Lam.5.19, byte tier) after eight verses without it, and what lies beyond that seam is a held-open close that is not decided here. The front seam is settled by the seam-pair edit adopted on the preceding item and needs no second adoption. The remaining findings verify, and their SCOPE changes with the new front seam, which is why they are re-specified rather than left as filed. Mark layer: this poem carries one mark, the poem-closing type at Lam.5.18, and none of the other type (sweep: 1 marked verse of 22), tier-3 weak and single-witness; a section mark after that verse does place it with what precedes, so the inference direction is right and only the driver wording fails - corroboration of a close already carried by a text signal is the most the layer may do. Signal keys: the mark-layer key belongs in prose only, and its hymnic namespace has no byte object inside the span, the second-person address standing at Lam.5.19 one verse past the close; and at Lam.5.18 the mountain is a place resumed by the third-masculine-singular בֽוֹ (oshb:Lam.5.18, byte tier), with no daughter-formula of any class anywhere in this poem, so the personification key has no byte object either. The position finding CHANGES VALUE with the new span and is re-derived here: with the row running Lam.5.11-Lam.5.18 the confession at Lam.5.16 - חָטָֽאנוּ (oshb:Lam.5.16, byte tier) - is the SIXTH of eight verses, not the fifth of seven and not the centre. The two subjects of Lam.5.13 also verify: the young men bore the mill and וּנְעָרִ֖ים ... כָּשָֽׁלוּ stumbled at the wood (oshb:Lam.5.13, byte tier), so a single clause about the young men drops one of them.

rulings.docket_item: adjudicate the candidate remedies carrying book-wide language into an explicit numbered corpus-wide order list, each with an arm, a scope and a test
rulings.grounds: Fifteen candidate remedies were reviewed for corpus scope. Thirteen name a defect class that recurs across rows and across parts and therefore cannot be discharged inside any one row's fix; each is issued below as a numbered order with its own arm, scope and test, and each executes as its OWN sweep over the whole 26-row corpus. Five candidate items are genuinely single-row and are DECLINED as corpus-wide orders, remaining row work orders where they were filed: the letter-order phrase misapplied to a letter set it does not govern in the third poem's opening triplets; the disclosure that Lam.3.17 admits both a direct address and a statement about the speaker's own soul; the ketiv/qere wording choice at the doubled note in Lam.4.3, which is one instance under the order that already covers that class; the missing inline reference beside the quoted translation line at Lam.4.7, which the standing quote-pairing arm already covers row by row; and the divine-name census correction at Lam.4.11. Each issued class was tested against bytes before being issued rather than being taken on the filing. The mark-layer signal keys are real and at least two stand in rows ruled in this slice, one naming the poem-closing mark in the opening poem and one naming it in the fifth. The count-object failures are real and reproduce: the remember-form census is 3 verses as a bare token and 2 as a petition imperative; the look-imperative census is 2 verses bare and 4 under the single-letter prefix test; and the first-person-singular suffix count at Lam.2.11 is 4 where 3 was filed. The straddle class is real at three separate seams verified here - the daughter-of-Zion formula at Lam.2.8 with Lam.2.10, the daughter-of-Jerusalem formula at Lam.2.13 with Lam.2.15, and the four-verse participant run at Lam.5.11-Lam.5.14. Five orders carry an exact, tool-decidable predicate; the other eight name a heuristic arm openly, because reading the pointed bytes or the governing relation of a sentence is what decides them and the staged extract carries no morphology layer to decide them mechanically. No order is folded into a row fix and no row fix discharges an order.

consequence.spec: Thirteen orders issued as CWO-1 through CWO-13 in the corpus_wide_orders list, each carrying its arm, predicate, scope and test. Five candidates declined as corpus-wide orders and left as row work orders, named in the grounds. EXECUTION PARITY: every order runs as its own sweep over all 26 rows and reports its own digits; a row-level repair that happens to satisfy an order does not discharge it, and no order may be recorded as satisfied by the row work orders enumerated on the other rulings of this slice. CWO-1, CWO-2, CWO-4, CWO-6 and CWO-10 are decidable by tool alone and are the first to run; the remaining orders name a heuristic arm and require a reading pass, and each states the exact screen that bounds it.
